REPORT ON Arrest of Russians.
Made by D. S. I. Sullivan. Forwarded by Chief Detective Officer
Sir,
Mr Metzler, Russian Vice-Consul, states that the Chinese
Police on the 2nd instant at the Commercial Press Printing
Works, North Honan Road, arrested Semeshko and a friend of his
named Ginsper, who has only been in Shanghai a couple of days.
The men were arrested purely on suspicion of being connected
with the paper the "Shanghai Chronicle", for the suppression of
which the assistance of the Chinese Police had been asked.
The two men were sent to the Russian Consulate and released
the same day.
I am, Sir,
your obedient servant,
J. Sullivan.
Detective Sub-Inspector.
Chief Detective Officer.
AM

REPORT ON The Shanghai Chronicle, new Russian weekly newspaper.

Made by D.S.I. Sullivan.    Forwarded by

Sir,

    Mr Grosse, Russian Consul' General states that at about
2 p.m. 30th ultimo he received a communication from the
Commercial Press, North Honan Road Extension; enclosing a
copy of a new Russian publication called the Shanghai Chronicle
and asking if there was any objection to its publication.
The Consul General read the paper and found that it contained
violent attacks on the Koltchak government and also libellous
and virulent attacks on the Russian Consul General in Shanghai.
The Consul General is accused of being a German, of speaking
German, and of being indifferent to the welfare of Russian
subjects in this port.

    Mr Grosse immediately intimated to the Commercial Press
Co. Ltd. that it was undesirable that the paper should be put
on the streets for sale, and directed that all the copies that
were left should be either sent to the Russian Consulate or
handed over to the Chinese Authorities. He also communicated
with General Lu Yung Ziang, Defence Commissioner of Shanghai
to the same effect. Those responsible for the appearance of
the paper, and the question of future issues, the Consul
General stated would be dealt with later, as there is a rule
that all Russian publications must be registered at the Russian
Consulate before they are allowed to be published.

由副巡官 Sullivan 制作。    经 转呈

先生，

    俄国总领事 Grosse 先生称，上月30日下午2点左右，他收到来自河南路延伸段商务印书馆的一份函件；信中附有一份名为《Shanghai Chronicle》的新俄文出版物副本，并询问对其出版是否有异议。
    总领事阅读了该报，发现其中包含对高尔察克政府的猛烈攻击，以及对上海俄国总领事的诽谤和恶毒攻击。
    总领事被指控为德国人、讲德语，并且对本港俄国侨民的福祉漠不关心。

    总领事表示，对该报出现负有责任的人员以及后续发行问题将在稍后处理，因为有一项规定要求所有俄国出版物在获准出版前必须在俄国领事馆注册。

REPORT ON Action re Bolshevist Newspaper.

Made by D.S.I. Givens. Forwarded by

Sir,
In response to a telephone message from the Russian
Consulate, I went there at 5.30 p.m. 30th June 1919, and met
D.S. Schmidt. We were handed a warrant authorising us to
search 88 Range Road, occupied by a Russian named Semeshko, and
seize all copies of the Russian paper called the Shanghai
Chronicle found therein.

Semeshko was out when we reached 88 Range Road, but we
seized 152 copies of the paper found in his room, and a
Russian Consular Representative who accompanied us took
possession of them. As we were leaving the premises, we met
D.S.I. Sullivan, who told us that he had discovered that
Semeshko had distributed copies of the paper to various news
agents, some of whom had redistributed them among their sub
agents. I then returned to the Central Station. A letter was
later sent to the Captain Superintendent by the Russian Consul
requesting to have steps taken to seize all copies of the
paper in Chinese shops. The contents of this letter were
communicated to the D.S.P., on whose instructions it was opened.
The latter gave instructions that a telephone message be sent to
all stations to warn shops against continuing to sell the papers
and to retain any copies in their possession until further
notice from the Police.

I am, Sir,
your obedient servant,
J.H. Givens D.S.I.

Shanghai, June 29th. Introduction.

To print a Russian Newspaper in Shanghai, without the necessities
is not light work. But we are not afraid of extra work and trouble,
to give the Russian Community here in Shanghai a neutral Newspaper,
commerce, local life, events etc. We know that the majority
of Russians here are Refugees, the present conditions in Russia
will not permit them to live there. Our paper might become an
enemy to some, and a friend to others. We are accused of being
Bolsheviks, but that is easy under present conditions. If you
fail to deliver your contract, you are a Bolshevik. If you asked
the Relief Fund, to change conditions in the Russian Printing
Establishment, you are a Bolshevik. If you have trouble with
the firm "Sergei Geiman & Co." you are a Bolshevik. Once you
are a Bolshevik, you have sorrows. But here in Shanghai we
have Courts, and it would be not difficult to prove otherwise.
We are not building Air-Castles, and we are not promising too
much, but we are promising the Russian Community a neutral Paper.

Who looks after the Russian Interests in Shanghai?
The military interests in Shanghai are guarded by the military
agent Colonel K.A.Kremenetohsky and his assistant Captain

three Russian Officials in Shanghai, the two above mentioned
military officers, and the newly joined Vice-Consul from Hankow,
Mr.H.A.Ivanoff.
Russian interests are not properly looked after here in Shanghai.
How could they be, if the Representatives of the Russian
Government are Germans, as for instance V.F.Grosse, who cannot

在上海，俄罗斯利益没有得到妥善维护。
如果俄罗斯政府的代表是德国人，例如 V.F. Grosse，他甚至不能清楚地讲俄语，又怎能得到妥善维护呢。

Vice-Consul Karl E.Metzler possesses apparently a second sight, or
has the gift to read other peoples hearts. A short time ago
one Mr.S. had the opportunity of getting employment at the
Russian Printing Establishment, as he was acquainted with, that
kind of work. What did Vice-Consul Metzler do? He notified
the management of the printing concern, that Mr.S. is a Bolshevik,
the consequence was, that they refused to engage him.
K.E.Metzler had no proof, that S. had had any dealings with the
Bolsheviks, except his gift of reading other people hearts.
Well, to make the story short, that is the kind of Officials we have got
at the Shanghai Consulate to look after the Russian interests.

副领事 Karl E. Metzler 显然拥有天眼通，或者
具有读心术的天赋。不久前，

K.E. Metzler 没有任何证据证明 S. 曾与布尔什维克
有任何往来，除了他读心术的天赋。
好吧，长话短说，这就是我们在上海领事馆拥有的、负责维护俄罗斯利益的官员类型。
